question.problem: On which of the following intervals can the intermediate value theorem be applied to the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{{x}^{2}-4x+4}?$
question.worked_solution:
The intermediate value theorem can be applied to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

The function is discontinuous at the values of $x$ which makes the denominator equal to zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero, we have ${x}^{2}-4x+4=0,$ which corresponds to $x=2.$ 

We conclude that the intermediate value theorem can be applied to the function $f(x)$ only on closed intervals that do not contain the point $x=2.$ 

From the given options, only the interval $[-1,1]$ is allowed. The intervals $(-2,1]$ and $[-1,2)$ are not closed, while $[0,2]$ and $[-1,3]$ contain the point $x=2.$
